question: Why is the supreme lord called Vāma in the arrangement of difference?
premises: The deity desires to make the withdrawal of beings its own.
To accomplish this, the deity constructs divisions among them.
The name Vāma is applied in the context of this arrangement of difference.
inference: Therefore, in the arrangement of difference, this supreme lord is called Vāma because he constructs divisions while intending their reabsorption.
plain_english: Desiring to take back these beings into himself, he constructs their divisions; therefore, in the arrangement of difference, this supreme lord is called Vāma.
